items.summary: Despite significant advances in terrestrial cellular network (4G LTE, 5G NR), and WiFi wireless local area network (WLAN) location services in recent years, centimeter-accurate real-time positioning services across federal geographic areas are currently available exclusively through global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) with differential correction systems (DCS). items.title: Trust-driven adaptive weighting for robust GNSS state Estimation under interference condition
items.summary: Reliable state estimation in Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) becomes challenging when measurement statistics are distorted by signal interference. Jamming, spoofing, multipath propagation, and environmental disturbances may significantly increase residual variance and introduce biases in pseudorange observations, which leads to degradation of navigation accuracy and loss of estimation reliability. Conventional robustness mechanisms typically rely on threshold-based fault detection, residual monitoring, or classical robust estimators. Although such approaches mitigate large outliers, they often employ binary measurement exclusion or purely statistical reweighting and therefore do not explicitly account for the reliability of individual measurement channels. This paper proposes a trust-driven adaptive weighting framework for GNSS state estimation under interference conditions. The method introduces a dynamic trust coefficient assigned to each measurement channel based on statistical quality assessment and risk-aware evaluation of its potential impact on the navigation solution. Residual variance is used to quantify measurement stability, while a channel risk factor incorporates geometric sensitivity and anomaly likelihood. The resulting trust coefficients regulate measurement influence through adaptive modification of the measurement covariance matrix within the Extended Kalman Filter.

items.summary: Profil vertikal atmosfer krusial untuk pemantauan cuaca, namun pengamatan radiosonde di Indonesia terkendala biaya dan cakupan spasial. Teknologi Global Navigation Satellite System Radio Occultation (GNSS RO) COSMIC-2 hadir sebagai alternatif efisien segala cuaca. Penelitian ini bertujuan memvalidasi data GNSS RO COSMIC-2 terhadap radiosonde di Indonesia menggunakan metode kuantitatif deskriptif dan komparatif. Analisis dilakukan pada 24 stasiun radiosonde dengan radius kolokasi 200 km, selang waktu dua jam, dan mencakup 11 lapisan tekanan (925–50 hPa) periode Juli 2020–Juni 2024. Data diolah dengan interpolasi logaritmik untuk menghitung rata-rata perbedaan serta standar deviasi. Hasil menunjukkan data COSMIC-2 memiliki kesesuaian yang baik pada parameter suhu dan kelembapan spesifik. Rata-rata perbedaan suhu nasional sebesar 0,102°C (standar deviasi 1,169°C), dengan Ranai sebagai wilayah paling sesuai (0,008°C) dan Medan tertinggi (0,214°C). items.title: Improved description of GNSS station velocity field uncertainty for high-precision applications
items.summary: Long-term deformation of the Earth’s surface inferred from Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) station position time series plays a central role in high-precision geodetic and geophysical applications, such as terrestrial reference frame realization, crustal deformation and strain rate estimation, or vertical land motion estimates for improved sea level change assessment. GNSS station position time series contain stochastic variations, often referred to as noise, that exhibit spatial correlations over distances of thousands of kilometers. The impact of these spatial correlations on the uncertainty of longterm station velocity estimates, however, remains poorly modeled and is therefore largely neglected. To address this limitation, we build on recent advances in the characterization and modeling of the spatio-temporal correlations of the noise in GNSS station position time series. We develop a multi-scale spatio-temporal noise correlation model and use it to derive the full covariance matrix of errors in a global station velocity field. Our results show that the spatio-temporally correlated noise induces significant and non-trivial correlations across station velocity errors, which depend not only on the distance between stations but also on the temporal overlap of the station position time series. Accounting for these spatial correlations could significantly improve the detection and uncertainty assessment of subtle long-term deformation signals. Plain Language Summary

items.title: Integrated Assessment of GNSS Observation Continuity and Positioning During the May 2024 Geomagnetic Superstorm
items.summary: The May 2024 geomagnetic superstorm disturbed the ionosphere and GNSS observations over Europe. We assessed data from 91 International GNSS Service (IGS) stations from 8 to 14 May 2024. The analysis combines vertical total electron content (VTEC) from BeiDou geostationary satellite (BDS GEO) links, the rate of TEC index (ROTI), short observation interruptions, and horizontal and vertical errors from single- and dual-frequency single-point positioning. The GEO links showed VTEC changes differed by location and strong evening fluctuations on 10 May and lower daytime VTEC on 11 May. Regional mean ROTI reached about 1.05 TECU/min near midnight on 10–11 May. The rate of short interruptions per valid satellite-hour increased after 18:00 UTC on 10 May. Rates in the later period were higher for all eight signals, but events were concentrated at a subset of stations. Single-frequency positioning errors also increased, with different timing across constellations and components. GPS L1 and Galileo E1 vertical errors reached about 8–9 m on 11 May, while the BDS B1C peak occurred on 12 May. The dual-frequency ionosphere-free single-point positioning series were more stable. These results show the value of assessing ionospheric changes, observation continuity, and positioning errors together.

items.title: Hard Sample Mining for GNSS Spoofing Detector via Physics-Based Meta-Learning Optimization
items.summary: GNSS spoofing detectors flag spoofing signals through sensing features such as carrier-to-noise density ratio and signal quality monitoring statistics. Training stronger detectors—and mapping detector performance boundaries—requires hard traction samples that systematically challenge those features, yet such samples are expensive to obtain under closed-loop replay and vary with the traction target. We propose Physics-Based Meta-Learning Optimization (PBMO) as a hard sample miner: it archives traction trajectories across traction targets, warm-starts a new traction target with Offline-RGPE and physics-based priors, and refines candidates with Physics-prior Guided Pattern Search (PhGPS). Hardness is scored by a conformal upper bound on the fraction of moving-variance windows that exceed channel thresholds. On a four-channel moving-variance (MV) detector, comparisons show that PBMO lowers the mean conformal upper bound by 30.7% relative to an unoptimized frequency-difference-lock strategy, and under the same online search budget remains below cold-start, nearest-neighbor, and mean-trajectory initializations. A USRP X310 wired loopback at one traction frequency preserves this ordering.

items.title: Topology-Consistent Trajectory Event Matching for GNSS-Denied Vehicle Initial Localization
items.summary: Vehicle initial localization under global navigation satellite system (GNSS)-denied conditions remains challenging because an odometry trajectory provides relative motion but no absolute road-network reference. Inspired by the coordinated use of self-motion information, recognizable route cues, and route continuity in biological navigation, this paper proposes a topology-consistent trajectory-event matching method. The method organizes odometry into ordered trajectory structure pairs formed by adjacent normal turning events and their intervening corridors, while a standard road-network map is automatically enhanced with internal direction-change points to construct corresponding map-side structures. Local candidates are retrieved according to direction, length, turning, and corridor-morphology consistency, and successive candidates are jointly confirmed under topological continuity. The confirmed discrete correspondence is then refined by local trajectory-image matching to estimate the continuous starting position. Experiments on KITTI-360 sequences 00, 08, and 09 with 135 starting positions yield an overall initialization success rate of 88.9%; successful trials achieve a mean error of 2.46 m and a median error of 2.29 m. The results show consistent performance across the evaluated road scenarios while indicating that sparse turning events and locally ambiguous road structures remain important limiting conditions.

items.title: A review of advanced low-cost GNSS technologies for navigation and precipitable water vapour monitoring
items.summary:
Abstract 
                   Low-cost Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers and antennas have emerged as promising alternatives to geodetic-grade equipment for precise positioning and atmospheric monitoring applications. Integrating multiple GNSS constellations, advanced positioning techniques such as Precise Point Positioning (PPP) and Real-Time Kinematic (RTK), and improved antenna designs have significantly enhanced consumer-grade GNSS hardware capabilities for Position, Navigation, and Timing services. This paper surveys PWV estimation using low-cost GNSS receivers, including smartphones (Huawei P40, Huawei Mate 20X), consumer chipsets (u-blox ZED-F9P, u-blox M8T, Piksi Multi, Unicorecomm Nebulas II), and low-cost antennas. Multi-constellation configurations (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, QZSS) consistently improved accuracy and reduced convergence times. PPP achieved sub-meter to centimeter-level accuracy; RTK demonstrated 2–5 cm horizontal accuracy. Tropospheric ZTD estimates agreed with geodetic equipment to 3–8 mm RMS, and PWV retrievals agreed with radiosonde and reanalysis products to within 1–3 mm. Low-cost GNSS has matured to near-geodetic performance for many applications. Antenna quality remains the primary accuracy differentiator multipath mitigation, ambiguity resolution for noisy receivers, this is a challenging task for improving positional accuracy for GNSS RTK users.

items.title: RANSAC-based iterative data refining method for multiple outliers in GNSS positioning
items.summary:
Abstract 
                   Effectively dealing with multiple outliers is indispensable for achieving reliable navigation and positioning performance in GNSS. The iterative data snooping (IDS) method is commonly used to identify outliers in a forward stepwise manner. Nevertheless, its effectiveness is often compromised by masking and swamping when multiple outliers are present. Recently, the iterative data refining (IDR) method was proposed as a backward alternative to IDS, which identifies potential inliers from the initial outlying set. However, its performance depends critically on the preset maximum number of suspected outliers (qmax), as this critically affects the quality of the initial outlying set. A large qmax covers all outliers at the expense of estimation accuracy, whereas a small qmax may fail to mitigate the masking and swamping effects. To address this dilemma, a dynamic adjustment strategy for qmax is adopted. Meanwhile, random sample consensus (RANSAC) is employed to evaluate whether the resulting inliers obtained by IDR still contain outliers, which guides the adjustment of qmax. Therefore, this paper proposes a RANSAC-based IDR method that dynamically adjusts qmax in a piecewise increasing manner. items.title: Evaluating the performance of GNSS RTK and UAV (drone) technologies under vrs mode in challenging environments
items.summary: Reliable geospatial data acquisition in obstructed environments is important for engineering surveying, but buildings, vegetation, multipath, and operational restrictions can reduce positioning reliability. This field study compared Global Navigation Satellite System Real-Time Kinematic (GNSS RTK), an RTK-enabled unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) using Virtual Reference Station (VRS) corrections, and handheld Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping (SLAM) across urban, forested, mixed-use, and semi-urban sites in Sri Lanka. Static GNSS and closed Total Station traverses established the reference coordinates. GNSS RTK was tested at all four sites, UAV RTK only in the urban corridor, and SLAM in the forested and mixeduse sites. Horizontal performance was assessed using root mean square error (RMSE), median, 95th percentile, maximum error, and availability. GNSS RTK RMSE values ranged from 0.064 to 0.121 m, UAV RTK recorded 0.106 m in the urban corridor, and SLAM recorded 0.160 m in the forest and 0.299 m in the mixed-use site. GNSS RTK gave the lowest errors where a stable FIX was available; UAV RTK provided rapid coverage, while SLAM maintained continuous mapping with higher drift-related error. Technology selection should therefore reflect required accuracy, coverage, access, and operating constraints.

items.title: Linearly-Constrained Adaptive Antenna Array for Ground-Based Radio Receivers of Global Navigation Satellite System
items.summary: Antenna arrays are widely used as the antennas of modern radio systems today. The ability to control the Radiation Pattern (RP) of such antennas underlies the operating principle of the Adaptive Antenna Arrays (AAA). These arrays suppress the signals from the interference sources whose frequency bands overlap with the frequency band of the desired (informational) signal. One of the most relevant applications of the AAAs is their usage in the ground-based equipment of the Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS). Such equipment primarily utilizes the AAAs known as the interference cancelers. Like any AAA, they suppress interferences but do not guarantee the receiving of a predetermined number of satellite signals which are necessary for solving the navigation task. This paper proposes to use a version of the linearly-constrained AAA. The constrain ensures a fixed value of the AAA RP towards zenith. The received signals from the satellites, which are located in this direction, provide the maximal signal-to-noise ratio due to the shortest distance from satellites to Earth. The value of the RP specified by the constraint is independent of the values of the AAA weights calculated during the adaptation. items.title: Detection-Aware Delayed Multi-Sensor Fusion for UAV GNSS Spoofing Mitigation: A Factor-Graph-Based Framework
items.summary: GNSS spoofing can progressively corrupt unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) navigation when manipulated position solutions are fused before integrity assessment. Existing detection methods often use dead-reckoning references such as visual–inertial odometry (VIO) without fully accounting for accumulated drift or GNSS-dependent global alignment. This paper presents a closed-loop software-in-the-loop (SITL) evaluation platform and a detection-aware delayed multi-sensor fusion framework for UAV GNSS spoofing mitigation. The platform couples state estimation, flight control, vehicle dynamics, and sensor feedback to enable Monte Carlo evaluation under realistic navigation–control interactions. A cumulative sum (CUSUM) detector monitors consistency between GNSS and drift-compensated VIO, while recent GNSS factors are quarantined and incorporated into a factor graph only after integrity screening. Experiments quantify false-alarm rate, detection probability, and latency across detector settings and spoofing deviation rates. Onboard implementation and controlled injection experiments further assess real-time feasibility and hardware transferability. Under the evaluated sensor conditions and gradual-drift attack model, a 10–15 s window yielded detection probabilities exceeding 96% for attacks with a deviation rate of 0.5 m/s, with an approximately 3% false-alarm rate. These findings demonstrate the framework’s potential for spoofing mitigation and the platform’s utility for closed-loop eval

items.summary: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals are the primary source of positioning, navigation and timing information in civil aviation. The open structure of civil GPS signals makes them inherently vulnerable to spoofing, and reported incidents affecting commercial aircraft have increased sharply since September 2023. Existing countermeasures either detect spoofing without restoring the navigation solution, depend on dedicated antenna arrays, or require offline training data, so none of them simultaneously satisfies the operational constraints of a standard single-antenna airborne receiver. items.title: STM32-Based Landmine Detection and GPS Localization Robotic Vehicle
items.summary: Autonomouslandmine detection remains a majorsafety challenge, as conventional manual methods expose personnel to hazardous environments, take considerable time, and may offer limited spatial tracking of detected threats. These limitations are particularly significant in military, humanitarian demining, and hazardous-terrain operations where accurate localization, autonomous navigation, and real-time monitoring are required. This thesis presents an Autonomous GNSS-Guided Mine Detection and Geofenced Monitoring Robot designed to autonomously survey a defined area and identify and spatially record potential metallic mine locations. The system provides dedicated access for field operators and administrators, where operators monitor robot movement, detected targets, and surveyed regions while administrators manage operational data, geofencing, and monitoring functions. The core mechanism combines GNSS positioning with centimeter-level correction, geofencing, barometric sensing, metal detection, and motor control to continuously calculate robot position and constrain movement within the predefined boundary, providing transparent rule-based navigation rather than relying on a black-box navigation model. Supporting features include autonomous movement, virtual fencing, boundary violation prevention, metal-detection marking, real-time position tracking, sensor-status monitoring, location logging, historical data visualization, and remote dashboard monitoring.

items.title: Neural Terrain Classification and Fuzzy Adaptive Covariance Tuning for Improved Outdoor Mobile Robot Localization
items.summary: Abstract Accurate and reliable localization is essential for autonomous outdoor mobile robots operating with low-cost sensors under varying terrain conditions. In such environments, the performance of an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) strongly depends on the appropriate selection of process- and measurement-noise covariance matrices, while fixed covariance parameters often fail to represent terrain-dependent uncertainty. The terrain-specific covariance parameters obtained offline using PSO are incorporated into a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system, which adapts the EKF covariance matrices online according to the estimated terrain type and its associated class-dependent reliability coefficient. The framework was experimentally validated on a wheeled mobile robot using commanded velocity inputs, low-cost Global Positioning System (GPS) measurements, and Real-Time Kinematic Global Navigation Satellite System (RTK-GNSS) reference trajectories collected over multiple outdoor terrain types. Compared with a baseline EKF using fixed covariance matrices, the proposed adaptive approach reduced the average root mean square error by 9.7% and the mean absolute error by 10.2%, with the largest improvements observed on deformable terrains. The results demonstrate that terrain-aware covariance adaptation provides an effective strategy for improving outdoor localization performance using low-cost sensing systems.

items.title: Onboard-navigation-aided federated fusion for telemetry tracking of high-dynamic flight-test targets
items.summary: Accurate guidance information is essential for telemetry antennas to maintain stable target tracking during flight tests. When the onboard navigation solution degrades or ground-based external tracking measurements are interrupted or abnormal, antenna pointing errors may increase and the telemetry link may become unstable. To improve the reliability of telemetry tracking, this paper applies adaptive federated filtering to a telemetry fusion tracking problem based on onboard navigation and ground-based external measurements. The downlinked SINS/GNSS integrated navigation solution is used as the reference solution at the ground station, and a reference-error state model is established. Ground-based radar measurements and optical measurements are then used to estimate and correct the position and velocity errors of the reference solution. The corrected target state is further converted into azimuth and elevation guidance angles for the telemetry antenna. In the adaptive fusion process, innovation-based fading factors and information allocation coefficients are used to adjust the reliability of different measurement branches and reduce the influence of abnormal measurements. Simulation results under representative disturbance scenarios verify the feasibility of the proposed method and indicate that the corrected target state can provide a more stable guidance reference for telemetry antenna tracking.

items.title: Rapid earthquake magnitude estimation from fuzzy C-means clustering-weighted fusion of seismogeodetic PGD and PGV
items.summary: Rapid and reliable earthquake magnitude estimation is essential for earthquake early warning and tsunami-impact assessment, particularly for large events for which conventional seismic estimates may saturate. Fuzzy C-means clustering is used to construct observation-dependent prior weights, while robust and geometry-aware weighting are introduced to reduce the effects of anomalous observations and uneven station distributions. In leave-one-earthquake-out validation, the PGD-only and PGV-only solutions yield mean absolute errors of 0.338 and 0.320 Mw, respectively, whereas joint PGD/PGV estimation reduces the error to 0.261 Mw. The full robust geometry-aware solution yields an MAE of 0.259 Mw. A two-event holdout test gives a fused mean absolute error of 0.194 Mw, although fusion does not outperform the better single-parameter estimate for every event. These results demonstrate that combining PGD and PGV provides the main improvement in magnitude estimation, while robust and geometry-aware weighting offer additional event-dependent benefits.

items.title: AGGO: Concept and realization of a geodetic observatory in South-America
items.summary: Geodetic observatories form the backbone of global geodetic reference frames. This article reviews the definition of the global geodetic reference system in terms of its origin, orientation, and scale, and its realization through reference frames. At geodetic observatories, reference points are materialized by instruments and survey markers. To achieve the highest possible accuracy, complementary measurement techniques are employed, often operating near the limits of what is technically feasible. Accordingly, a geodetic observatory brings together complex instruments, including a radio telescope for very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), a satellite laser ranging (SLR) system, receiving stations for global navigation satellite systems (GNSS), atomic clocks, absolute and superconducting gravimeters, and complementary sensors. The spatial relationships between the reference points of these instruments are determined through precise local surveys (local ties). The current instrumentation of the Argentine-German Geodetic Observatory (AGGO) is described as an example of the range of measurement techniques needed to establish and maintain a reference site within the global geodetic reference frame. Measurement data collected at AGGO are made freely available through international services.
